sm: This is the start of the Williamson County wrestling media day interviews. A first coach says his favorite part of coaching is watching athletes grow as wrestlers and people over a season, and says leadership means walking the walk. A wrestler named Briona wants to make state. Brentwood's coach Smith says the team is reloading after graduating nine seniors, with the motto strive for success, and his wrestler Charlie wants to become a state placer. Coach Smith says wrestling teaches you to bounce back, and both name Ravenwood as the rival they most look forward to. Page's coach Benji Gray says great wrestlers live the lifestyle, and Page returns nine boys starters and added former state medalist Libby.

Libby says she wants to get back on the podium and that her new team feels like a big family. Summit's coach Miller says the team goal is always the state duals, and wrestler Addison wants to win state and recalls winning it in eighth grade. The coach says he was born into wrestling, since his father was a well known coach at Cleveland. Fairview's new girls team is described as young and enthusiastic, and a wrestler cites Olympic gold medalist Sarah Hildebrandt as her inspiration. Ravenwood's coach Callie says her goal is for girls to wrestle, have fun and be safe, after her own difficult high school experience. Her wrestler Emery finished second at state last year and wants to win it in her final season.

A Ravenwood wrestler names her dad as her biggest inspiration. Her coach wants wrestlers to leave as people of character who enjoy the process, and says the team focuses on daily improvement rather than wins and losses. Their favorite memories include a state championship, a first-year wrestler finally winning his eleventh match, and two teammates reaching state. Independence's coach Drew wants more wins, more state qualifiers and some hardware, and wrestler Doria wants to reach the state finals after first making state last year. Fairview's coach Biff asks for grit, discipline and determination. Fairview has missed state duals three years in a row by one match, and aims to qualify all fourteen weight classes for individuals. His wrestler Cole wants a state title.

Coach Biff says he never wrestled as a kid and got into coaching through his son, because he wants to mentor young men. Cole hopes for a rematch with a Station Camp wrestler. Summit's coach says the goals are the same every year, a region title and a return to the state duals and state finals, while always chasing Cleveland. A Summit wrestler wants to win state, and the coach defines leadership as showing up, doing right when nobody is watching and helping younger wrestlers. Nolensville's coach Melzoni wants to build on last year, and says wrestlers control only effort, attitude and aggression. Jake aims to win state. An Independence coach says his seniors had the same head coach all four years, and his slogan is embrace the uncomfortable.

A wrestler says he wants to be the hardest working person in the room. Franklin's coach bases the program on effort, competition and leadership, and says he grew up in Franklin wrestling. His first win as head coach was eighty-four to nothing over Rockvale. He says Franklin has state finalist Carson Gamble and state medalist Maddox McCullen, in a tough district with Independence, Summit and Nolensville. Both wrestlers name Summit and Nolensville as the toughest duals. Ravenwood's coach Peck says the team feels insulted by Page and Franklin, and was stung when Page knocked them out of state duals. JD wants a state championship. Centennial's Brandon Montero hopes to place at state, and credits his older brother as motivation.
